so i wrote a brief "review" of far cry 4 a little while ago after revisiting the game. i have since downloaded the valley of the yeti dlc and wanted to do a quick review of that, too.

you start off after a plane you're in crashes and the pilot has been captured by mysterious unknown bad guys. all your equipment is gone and so are all the skills you developed (like using syringes or searching automatically after a take down.) it turns out there is some group that is in charge of the area and are really into the demon yalung and are being affected by a unique environmental effect in what seems like a detrimental way. there is also some "relic" that is so attractive that yuma lau, pagan min's second in command, sent a group to this area over a year ago that have gone missing. also yetis.

there are a few differences between the main game and this dlc. for one thing some of the skills such as elephant riding aren't even available because of there being no elephants. also there's no quick travel which isn't the worst thing because the map isn't that large but there were a couple of times i wish i had it- specifically there seems to be a ton of wolves running around and fighting them off used up a lot of ammo which was annoying when i was trying to conserve it.

it also deals with weapon unlocks in a different manner. you'll see yellow pistol icons on the map where different weapons are located. you just have to locate and equip the gun and it will unlock back at your base. you can even equip the gun then immediately drop it to switch back to your previous weapon if you want and the item will still be available to you at your base. i like this idea but some of the weapons were just sitting around with no defenders or anything and i think it would have been more fun to have to work to get them. since there weren't any radio towers or bases to clear it did provide a reason to explore the map and i kind of liked the way it worked.

there is another thing that i think happened with weapons but i could be wrong so take this with a grain of salt. early on i came across a bad guy out in the woods shooting at stuff and got the jump on him. he had my favorite sniper rifle (the sa-50) and i picked it up because i hadn't unlocked a sniper rifle yet. when i got back to base this gun was available to me. now i know for sure that in far cry 3 picking up a weapon didn't unlock it for you in this manner because in a similar circumstance i picked up a sniper rifle before it was unlocked but when i died later it was no longer available to me. i'm not sure if the same thing happens in far cry 4 because i don't remember a circumstance when it happened but i think it's a good idea if it's a new one.

there is also a base mechanic where you have to develop and defend a base you acquire from the bad guys. this was fun but i enjoyed clearing bases and climbing radio tower more and missed this activity in the dlc. i think it would be a good idea if they could incorporate both in a future game if there are any planned.

i'm not finished with the dlc yet and am enjoying it as i really liked far cry 4 a lot. (far cry primal was o.k. but i didn't like the setting as much as i thought i might and prefer the more traditional modern setting.) there seems to be a fair amount of content to the dlc as i've played it for several nights and am still not done so i would suggest anyone that likes far cry 4 try it out.
